name: The Mom Test Conversational Protocol
phase: Customer Discovery and Problem Validation Tactics
hypothesis: We believe that [target customer segment] experiences severe operational inefficiency when [executing specific task]. We will verify this by conducting 12 conversational interviews focusing exclusively on past actions, and consider it validated if at least 8 of 12 respondents independently describe a dedicated, imperfect workaround they used within the last 14 days without prompting.

plan.label: Preparation
plan.text: Write five prompts about past events; strip every reference to a solution, a business or a hypothetical.

plan.label: Execution
plan.text: Run 30-minute interviews anchored in the last time they did the task, what it cost, and what they tried first.

plan.label: Data collection
plan.text: Transcribe verbatim; label each line historical behaviour, speculation or feeling, and drop speculation.

planFull.label: Preparation
planFull.text: Formulate 5 open-ended inquiry prompts anchored strictly in historical occurrences. Strip all references to prospective solutions, business concepts, and hypothetical feature sets.

planFull.label: Execution
planFull.text: Conduct 30-minute semi-structured interviews. Anchor discussions in past events using prompts such as: "Walk me through the last time you completed [task]," "How much time or budget did resolving that bottleneck consume?" and "What alternative approaches failed?".

planFull.label: Data collection
planFull.text: Record the dialogue verbatim. Classify every statement into three categories: historical behavior, stated forward-looking speculation, or emotional frustration. Disregard speculative statements entirely during synthesis.

warning.label: Courtesy Bias
warning.text: Show your concept and interviewees politely affirm it to avoid friction, manufacturing validation.

warningFull: When interviewers disclose their product concept, interviewees offer polite affirmations to avoid interpersonal friction, generating an illusion of validation.
